items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: In Budgetary terms, what is Revenue deficit?
o: The amount by which Revenue Expenditure is more than Revenue receipts
Excess of Revenue Expenditure on all receipts
Excess of all expenditure on all receipts
items.x: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts, i.e. the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.

items.src: UPSC Preliminary 2016
items.s:
There has been a persistent deficit budget year after year. Which action/actions of the following can be taken by the Government to reduce the deficit?

A. Reducing revenue expenditure

B. Introducing new welfare schemes

C. Rationalizing subsidies

D. Reducing import duty
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
items.x: Cutting revenue expenditure and rationalising subsidies reduce the deficit; new welfare schemes and lower import duty would widen it.

items.x: In the December 2008 stimulus package the CENVAT rate was cut by 4 percentage points, from 14% to 10% (cut further to 8% in February 2009).

items.src: UPSC Civil Services 2011
items.s: Which one of the following statements appropriately describes the "fiscal stimulus"?
o: It is a massive investment by the Government in manufacturing sector to ensure the supply of goods to meet the demand surge caused by rapid economic growth
It is an intense affirmative action of the Government to boost economic activity in the country
It is Government's intensive action on financial institutions to ensure disbursement of loans to agriculture and allied sectors to promote greater food production and contain food inflation
It is an extreme affirmative action by the Government to pursue its policy of financial inclusion.
items.x: A fiscal stimulus is an intense affirmative action of the Government (tax cuts, higher spending) to boost economic activity, as in the 2008-09 packages; it is not tied to manufacturing, farm credit or financial inclusion. (Official UPSC key: b.)

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-I Panchayat Secretary (Grad
items.s:
Consider the following statements:

A. In Andhra Pradesh, the share of agriculture is increasing in the State's GSDP

B. The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation is the nodal agency for Special Economic Zones in the State.

C. IT sector is the fastest growing sector.

D. Amrut Solar Power Plant is operating at Kadiri in Kurnool district.

items.x: D is wrong: the solar park at Kadiri (NP Kunta) is in Anantapur (now Sri Sathya Sai) district, not Kurnool. B is correct (APIIC is the nodal agency for SEZs). 'A and D' is the only option containing D; the key treats A (rising agriculture share) as incorrect, which depends on the year taken.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: Which of the following formula is related to the distribution of electricity between the Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
items.x:
Most keys: Gadgil Formula. Strictly: APRA 2014 Twelfth Schedule (C, para 6) allots central generating station power by actual energy consumption of the last 5 years; no formula is named (src/ap-reorganisation/apra.txt).
Exam keys answer the Gadgil Formula. The Act itself does not name it: the Twelfth Schedule shares central generating station power by actual consumption over the last five years. The Gadgil Formula (1969) shared Plan assistance; Mahalanobis, Tendulkar and Arria are unrelated.
